root_cause.text: The igc TSN-mode transmit buffer configuration allocated an excessive 7 KB TX packet buffer per queue in `IGC_TXPBSIZE_TSN`, which under heavy packet timestamping load led the hardware TX unit to hang.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and CVE state that “The previous 7 KB per queue caused TX unit hangs under heavy timestamping load,” and the patch changes `IGC_TXPBSIZE_TSN` in `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igc/igc_defines.h` from `IGC_TXPBxSIZE(7)` for all four queues to `IGC_TXPBxSIZE(5)`, noting that 5 KB matches the I225/I226 TSN recommendation.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The igc driver's TSN-mode TX packet buffer configuration over-allocated 7 KB to each TX queue in IGC_TXPBSIZE_TSN, a hardware-unsafe setting that can make the TX unit hang under heavy timestamping load.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly states "The previous 7 KB per queue caused TX unit hangs under heavy timestamping load" and the patch fixes this by changing IGC_TXPB0SIZE/1SIZE/2SIZE/3SIZE in drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igc/igc_defines.h from 7 to the manual-recommended 5 KB per queue.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence that 7 KB is a "hardware-unsafe setting" is not present in the CVE, commit message, or patch. Those sources only say that the previous 7 KB per queue configuration caused TX unit hangs under heavy timestamping load and that 5 KB matches the manual recommendation. Calling it "hardware-unsafe" is an unsupported extrapolation. Also, the proposed root cause is weakly framed as the configuration value itself, without explaining the underlying reason beyond restating the symptom/fix.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct the TSN transmit packet buffer size constants to match the I225/I226 hardware manual recommendations.
intent_record.what: The diff adds a comment above IGC_TXPBSIZE_TSN indicating the TSN value follows the I225/I226 Software User Manual Section 7.5.4, and changes the IGC_TXPBSIZE_TSN macro so that TXPB0SIZE through TXPB3SIZE are each set from 7 to 5 while leaving IGC_OS2BMCPBSIZE(4) unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, TSN-specific transmit packet buffer sizing is reduced for each of the four TX packet buffers, changing the hardware configuration programmed when the TSN preset is used so it matches the documented manual values instead of allocating larger per-queue buffers.

grouping_result.intent: Correct the TSN transmit packet buffer size constants to match the I225/I226 hardware manual recommendations.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is caused by an excessive TSN-mode TX packet buffer allocation, and this change directly fixes the TSN transmit buffer size constants to the hardware-recommended values.

candidates.rationale: This macro definition is the direct source of the faulty TSN transmit buffer configuration; it defines the constant whose excessive per-queue allocation caused the TX hang.
This line assigns 7 KB to TX packet buffers 0-2 in TSN mode, directly embodying the excessive per-queue buffer sizing described in the root cause.
This line assigns 7 KB to TX packet buffer 3 as part of the same TSN-mode macro, completing the excessive 7 KB-per-queue configuration that could trigger TX unit hangs.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line directly encodes the TSN-mode transmit packet buffer allocation of 7 KB for TX packet buffers 0-2. The root cause states that the excessive 7 KB per queue allocation in TSN mode led to TX hardware hangs under heavy packet timestamping load.

This line completes the same TSN-mode macro by assigning 7 KB to TX packet buffer 3. Together with the previous line, it forms the excessive TSN transmit buffer configuration identified as the root cause of the vulnerability.
